data.name: Tower of Eglathia
data.detailed_description:
The Tower does not care why you came. It has swallowed paladins, thieves, and scholars. It has taken the proud and the desperate - you cannot win, adventurer.

Somewhere above the twenty-first floor, something still waits — and a demon in your ear will help you reach it, if you are foolish enough to listen.

Tower of Eglathia is a turn-based traditional roguelike: one life, a new tower every run, and every prayer, potion, and step a bet you might not get to make twice.

Choose who you were before the door. Choose Barbarian, Mystic, Assassin, or the forbidden Eglathian bloodline. Then climb until the floor — or the demon — takes you. Inspired by the dark-fantasy world of Eglathia.

Four Paths. Fifty Abilities. One Life.

  • Barbarian — Crush enemies with raw strength and brutal melee power.

  • Mystic — Master devastating spells, shields, and elemental fury.

  • Assassin — Strike from shadows with precision, poison, and deadly speed.

  • Eglathian — Channel ancient bloodline powers that blend magic and martial prowess.

Mix trees or master one. Spell-slinging berserker, shadow mage, or pure Eglathian — the tower does not grade on style.

The Tower Itself

  • 21+ floors of escalating danger, procedurally generated every run

  • 60+ unique monsters — kobolds and evil eyes through mature dragons and demon generals

  • Hundreds of items — enchanted weapons, armor, scrolls, potions, wands, rings, amulets, artifacts

  • Turn-based tactical combat — position, resources, and one more step

  • Difficulties: Easy, Normal, Hard, and Doom

  • Hardcore permadeath — glory is earned; the Wall of Heroes keeps the receipts

Risk Everything

  • Altars — pray for favor, donate for magic, or desecrate for riches. Divine wrath is not a rumor

  • Fountains — liquids that heal, harm, or grant power you may not understand until you drink

  • Scrolls and wands — one-use spells and tools with charges

  • Potions — drink, throw, or pour. Identification is part of the fight

Version 2.0

  • Eglathian skill tree — 15+ hybrid abilities (Shadow Bolt, Triune Convergence, Blade Echo, and more)

  • Class specialization bonuses at levels 1, 5, 10, 15, and 20

  • 29 Steam Achievements

  • Wall of Heroes — Hardcore runs, legendary and embarrassing

  • Quests and lore — demons, ghosts, and the tower’s unfinished business

The demon whispers. The floors never repeat. The Wall of Heroes remembers who made it — and who didn’t. The Tower of Eglathia is still standing. Most who entered it are not. Eglathia, the novel, is available on Amazon.

reviews.review:
As a huge roguelike nerd that has been thoroughly invested in the genre for over 20 years I sadly can't recommend Tower of Eglathia. 

It feels like I'm playing one of those games that came on the CD's with 250 free shareware games back in the mid 90s. The game is buggy, lacks certain features and the game engine itself feels clunky and archaic.

[b]Here are some examples of what stood out to me:[/b]

[*] When you open up any screen in the game (be it character info, inventory, checking the settings, reading a scroll and so on) the game opens up a totally new game window. All screens in the game opens up a new window.
[*] You can't turn sound effects or music off (you can however lower the volume but you'll still be able to barely hear the game which can be annoying)
[*] Below average quality sound effects.The sound effects become tiresome to listen to as they repeat constantly, there's very little variation.
[*] Buttons can't be remapped. 
[*] There are no resolution/video settings except for turning fullscreen on/off. 
[*] The text font is tiny and you sadly can't increase the font size. People with bad eye sight will have huge problems reading the in-game text.  
[*] You can't turn off the tutorial messages and they pop up during every new game. The in-game achievements and its notifications can also not be turned off.
[*] Some tooltips are so long that they leave the screen, making it impossible to read the whole text.
[*] There's also a FMV introduction video with the developer cosplaying as a character within the game. I personally don't mind it (even though it's cheesy), but it's without a doubt something that will turn a lot of people off. The introduction video can't be turned off and will play every single time you start a new game. It's possible to skip the video though.
[*] Spelling errors.

Simply put: There are a lot of really weird game and engine design choices that just makes the game a lot worse then what it could've been. In its current state I simply can't recommend the game even though it's pretty cheap as there are far better roguelikes out there that are also free [b](Games like: DCSS, ToME v4, Brogue, DoomRL, ADOM, Cataclysm:DDA, NetHack, Angband, Sil, Infra Arcana, UnReal World etc.)[/b].
reviews.developer_response:
The following have been fixed/changed that you have brought up:

* Changing music or sound volume all the way to the left will turn music and sound off completely.
* You can now turn off the tutorial, achievement, and video messages.

* I'd love to know what spelling errors you found so I can correct them as well as how you think the buttons should be allowed to be mapped, what tool tips are too long, and what would make the sound better for you. Thanks again.
